info.title: Orbit Gateway API
info.description: The HTTP API of the active Orbit Gateway. The CLI and the PHP SDK send every fleet command through these endpoints over WireGuard. See [Using the API](/api/overview) for transport, authentication, envelopes, and errors.

servers.description: The active Gateway on the private WireGuard network, resolved by Orbit private DNS.

post.description: The `orbit-agent` on a managed Node calls this endpoint to join its own presence channels. The Gateway signs member `agent.{id}` on `presence-node.{id}` or `presence-node-logs.{id}` only for a request from that Node's WireGuard address that carries the Node's agent secret. The response carries the Pusher `auth` and `channel_data` values.

404.description: Realtime is not configured (`realtime.not_configured`).

401.description: The request carries no agent secret (`agent.secret_required`).

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`), its agent secret does not match (`agent.secret_invalid`), its Node is not eligible for an agent (`agent.node_ineligible`), or it asked for another Node's channel (`agent.channel_forbidden`).

422.description: The JSON body is not an object, has duplicate or unknown members, or fails validation (`validation.failed`).

post.summary: Report one fact the agent observed
post.description: The `orbit-agent` on a managed Node sends one fact it observed, of kind `host`, `units`, `checkout`, `checkouts`, `packages` or `ufw`, when it changed and every 10 minutes. The Gateway stores the latest fact per Node, kind and subject; a `checkouts` index deletes the checkouts it omits. An unchanged fact writes nothing. The answer is 204 either way.

subject.description: The checkout path for `checkout`, the Tool Manager name for `packages`; refused for other kinds.

observed_at.description: The agent's time, to the second or millisecond, in UTC.

data.description: The fact, as the Node agent reference defines each kind.

204.description: The Gateway stored the fact, or it was unchanged.

413.description: The request is larger than 1 MiB (`agent.fact_too_large`).

422.description: The data does not match the kind, or an `egress` fact came from a Node that is no task VM host or names another bridge than its own (`agent.fact_not_expected`).

401.description: The request carries no agent secret (`agent.secret_required`).

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`), its agent secret does not match (`agent.secret_invalid`), or its Node is not eligible for an agent (`agent.node_ineligible`).

get.summary: List the live log streams the agent reads
get.description: The `orbit-agent` on a managed Node calls this endpoint to learn which logs to read for live log streams: when it joins its log channel, after each `log-streams.changed` event, and every 15 seconds while it reads a stream. The Gateway identifies the Node from the WireGuard address and the agent's bearer secret, and lists at most 16 open streams whose source is on that Node, each with its ID, `lines`, and one `laravel`, `journal`, or `docker` source that the Gateway resolved from its own records.

lines.description: The number of earlier lines to send first.

process_id.description: `docker`: the Process ID in the container name and label.

401.description: The request carries no agent secret (`agent.secret_required`).

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`), its agent secret does not match (`agent.secret_invalid`), or its Node is not eligible for an agent (`agent.node_ineligible`).

get.description: The `orbit-agent` on a managed Node calls this endpoint to find its Reverb connection. The Gateway identifies the Node from the WireGuard address and the agent's bearer secret, and returns the Reverb URL, serving address, and app key, the Node's `presence-node.{id}` channel, and the agent's `agent.{id}` member ID. Connection values are null when broadcasting is not configured. While the websocket role is assigned but no Reverb serves it, for example no serving report in the last 60 seconds, it answers 503 `realtime.not_serving`, so the agent retries on its back-off.

address.description: Address that serves Reverb on port 443.

log_channel.description: The Node's log channel, `presence-node-logs.{id}`, for live log streams.

503.description: The websocket role is assigned, but no Reverb serves it (`realtime.not_serving`).

401.description: The request carries no agent secret (`agent.secret_required`).

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`), its agent secret does not match (`agent.secret_invalid`), or its Node is not eligible for an agent (`agent.node_ineligible`).

get.description: The `orbit-agent` on a managed Node calls this endpoint at start and every 60 seconds to learn what to watch: `services`, the systemd services of the Node's roles, `workspaces`, the task checkouts that `agent:workspaces` lists, and `apps_root`, the apps path of an active app-dev Node. The Gateway identifies the Node from the WireGuard address and the agent's bearer secret.

services.description: Systemd services of the Node's roles, such as `caddy.service`.

apps_root.description: The apps path of an active app-dev Node, whose checkouts the agent reports; null otherwise.

applications.description: By Project slug, the application directory inside a checkout when it is not the checkout root, such as `server/web`.

tools.description: Each active Tool Manager with the candidate paths of its package state.

401.description: The request carries no agent secret (`agent.secret_required`).

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`), its agent secret does not match (`agent.secret_invalid`), or its Node is not eligible for an agent (`agent.node_ineligible`).

get.summary: List the task checkouts the agent watches
get.description: The `orbit-agent` on a managed Node calls this endpoint every 60 seconds to learn which task checkouts to watch. The Gateway identifies the Node from the WireGuard address and the agent's bearer secret, and lists the Instances on that Node that hold the workspace of an unfinished task group, at most 64, with the checkout path, the Project's default branch as `base`, and the Instance's starting commit as `start`. The list is empty while the tasks extension is disabled.

instance_id.description: The Instance that holds the task workspace.

path.description: The absolute checkout path on the Node.

base.description: The Project's default branch, which the diff counts are read against.

start.description: The Instance's starting commit, or null.

401.description: The request carries no agent secret (`agent.secret_required`).

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`), its agent secret does not match (`agent.secret_invalid`), or its Node is not eligible for an agent (`agent.node_ineligible`).

delete.description: Stops the collector Process for the whole fleet, withdraws collector.ai-router.orbit and its certificate, deletes the stored CLIProxyAPI management key and the read and control tokens, and hides provider reads. Setting up again needs the management key. The Redis connection and Valkey data stay. Refuses with extension.required (409) while the tasks extension is enabled. Destroy refuses with ai_router.cutover_pending while the release cutover is pending.

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`) or lacks Node access to the target (`node_access.required`).

409.description: A guard refused the change and the Gateway changed nothing; `error.code` names the guard. A disabled extension returns HTTP 409 (`extension.disabled`).

post.description: Deploys one collector Process and publishes https://collector.ai-router.orbit after a Redis Database connection for shared Valkey is in place. Fails closed when that connection is missing, is not Redis, or names a Node without the database role. A custom proxy Route that already serves the collector hostname on that Node is withdrawn in the same Caddy reload and removed; any other Route on that name fails with ai_router.hostname_taken. The response never includes tokens or the management key. Setup refuses with ai_router.cutover_pending while the release cutover is pending.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A permanent key scoped to this operation kind, target and input. The same request returns the existing operation with HTTP 202; a changed identity returns operation.idempotency_conflict (409).

post.description: Pin another Plausible version for the analytics role.

version.description: Plausible Community Edition version, for example 3.2.1

202.description: Accepted. The operation is queued; follow it with `operation:show`.

503.description: The Gateway has no queue (`operation.queue_unavailable`) and recorded nothing, or it could not queue the job (`operation.dispatch_failed`) and ended the operation as failed.

403.description: The caller is not an active WireGuard peer (`peer.identity_unknown`) or lacks Node access to the target (`node_access.required`).

409.description: A guard refused the change and the Gateway changed nothing; `error.code` names the guard. The key already belongs to another target or input (`operation.idempotency_conflict`), or another operation holds the target (`operation.target_busy`).

422.description: The JSON body is not an object, has duplicate or unknown members, or fails validation (`validation.failed`). A malformed Idempotency-Key also returns `validation.failed`.

get.description: Lists the registered T3 servers whose registering Node the caller has node access to, with their URL, server version, registration time, and admin session expiry. `status` is `session_expired` when the server must register again; cleanup_pending records a newer registration revision awaiting Swamp cleanup. A server of a container Instance names its `instance_id` and the container's `power_state` (`running` or `stopped`); it also supplies `project_id`, `project_name`, `project_slug`, `instance_name`, `node_name`, and `instance_url` for Conn to display Orbit facts while container T3 servers stay stock. `instance_url` follows the Instance URL rule (authoritative Route, otherwise first Route, or null without a Route), separately from the T3 `url`. Other servers have null for all eight Instance fields.

get.description: Requires enabled Conn and node access to the Node that serves the T3 server, else `node_access.required` (403). Only for the T3 server of a container Instance. The client presents access_token as its bearer to url directly. Without a held session it admits one conn.session_hold, in which the Gateway mints a pairing link with its admin session and redeems it on T3's pairing endpoint, and returns that Operation with 202; concurrent first reads return the same Operation. Follow conn:operation:show, then read again. It ignores Idempotency-Key, so a repeated read answers the current state. Refusals: conn.environment_not_instance, conn.environment_asleep (no held session while the Instance sleeps), conn.session_expired, instance.removal_conflict (409). On a 401 from the server, read again.

patch.description: Requires node access to at least one Node. Changes sections of the settings document, each with the version the client last read: `{"sections": {"appearance": {"version": 3, "value": {...}}, "devices.iphone": {"version": 0, "value": null}}}`. A section is `workspaces`, `appearance`, `attachedThreads`, or `devices.<type>`; an unknown name returns `validation.failed` (422). A section with no recorded version reads as 0, including one written before sections had versions. A null value removes any section but `workspaces`; a new attached thread whose environment is gone or not visible to the caller returns `validation.failed` (422), while a thread already attached may be carried by any caller (/reference/conn#attached-threads); an empty string returns `validation.failed` (422). The request is all or nothing: if any section is at another version it returns `conn.settings_version_conflict` (409) with `details.current_version` and `details.sections`, the current version of each section sent, and writes nothing. A write adds 1 to each section version and to the document version.

get.description: Requires node access to at least one Node. By default, preserves the pre-directory set for installed Conn clients: Projects with a reachable active container default and a seed snapshot. Optional include_unavailable accepts 1/true/0/false (absent=false); true lists all reachable Projects as project:list does. Invalid include_unavailable values return validation.failed (422). Unknown query fields are ignored. Both forms retain instance_domain_suffix, ordered checks, cloneable and cloneable_reason, in ascending slug order, with no defined relative order for slugs that compare equal. The compatible set can include a later technical refusal; cloneable is unchanged. Node fields and suffix are null when hidden. Check again re-reads without cached eligibility. get.description: Requires access to the ready default Instance. Reads at most 100 matching remote branches: default first, then bytewise ascending names. query is an optional case-insensitive substring of at most 255 characters; leading or trailing whitespace is refused. Further matches are omitted; narrow query. Each branch names its newest open PR from this repository (creation time, then number descending) and the lowest-id visible matching Instance. Source credentials plus git share ten seconds; PR credentials plus at most five pages of 100 open PRs share a separate ten seconds. Installation facts and CLI tokens are reused within the request. External reads take at most twenty seconds total plus local work; PR failure or overflow keeps branches with null PRs and meta.pull_requests_unavailable=true. Non-GitHub sources have null PRs. See /reference/conn#threads-in-an-orbit-project.

post.description: Requires node access to the Node of the Project's default Instance. Admits instance.create of a clone named `name` on that Node, as instance:create does, and returns the Operation (202) whose target_id is the new Instance. Follow it with conn:operation:show. The same name again resumes the caller's own clone; a name another device's create holds returns `instance.name_taken` (409). A name that resolves to `default` returns `validation.failed` (422); a Project without a ready container default returns `instance.default_missing` (409). Optional branch is a closed object: mode new requires from; mode existing requires name. One credentialed remote-head read shares ten seconds with credentials, before reservation. Refusals: branch.in_use (409; details.instance or {} when hidden); branch.not_found (422; details.field branch.name or branch.from); branch.exists (422; details.field name and details.branch); source.head_unavailable (502). Explicit results add branch and base_branch (null for existing). Dependencies and build come from the default seed; no setup reruns. get.description: Requires node access to at least one Node. Only a list that names `instance` reads that one server through first, while the operator switch ORBIT_CONN_THREAD_INDEX_POLL is on, the server runs and its last read is older than 10 seconds, waiting at most 0.5 seconds; an asleep server keeps its last rows. The Gateway runs the extension's enable hook first and turns the switch on only after it succeeds; a failed hook leaves the switch off and returns the hook's error. parameters.name: node
parameters.description: Numeric Node ID. List only that Node; omit it for every Node the caller may address.

get.description: Returns the firewall rules of the Nodes the caller can reach, or of the one Node in `node`, ordered by Node and then in the order UFW checks them. It reads Gateway state only and does not SSH. `managed=1` adds the `orbit:` rules Orbit intends on each Node: WireGuard member trust, public SSH recovery only while no active role has closed it, then each active role, the task VM image peers on a task VM host, and Metrics. No request adds, changes, or removes one of them. `live=1` adds a `match` to each rule and the Node's `live` block, from the last `ufw` fact its orbit-agent reported. Until the agent reports UFW, `backend_status` is `unverifiable` and every `match` is `unverifiable`. While the agent is offline, `live.possibly_outdated` is true.

agent.description: With `live`: the liveness of the Node agent. Null for a Node that runs no observing agent.

since.description: The time of the last agent event while it is offline.

rules.description: The operator rules in the order UFW checks them. With `live`, each has a `match`.

match.description: With `live`: whether the Node has the rule. `missing` also covers a firewall that is off or not installed.

managed.description: With `managed`: the rules Orbit intends on the Node after role converge. No request adds, changes, or removes one.

name.description: The `orbit:` comment that identifies the rule in UFW.

role.description: The role that needs the rule, or null for a baseline rule the Node still intends.

interface.description: The interface the rule is limited to; `orbit` is the WireGuard interface.

match.description: With `live`: the match with the Node.

live.description: With `live`: how the Node compares with the rules.

backend_status.description: Whether UFW answered on the Node. `unverifiable` means no orbit-agent UFW observation exists.

possibly_outdated.description: True while the Node agent is offline, so the matches may be stale.

unmatched.description: Live rules that no listed rule explains: `unmanaged`, or `drift` from a rule with a known comment. Rules of Orbit itself appear only with `managed`.

post.summary: Prove a command on the task VM

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A permanent key scoped to this operation kind, binding caller and command as well as target and input. The same request returns the existing operation with HTTP 202; a changed identity returns operation.idempotency_conflict (409).

post.description: Starts keyed proof.verify for one command on the task VM that calls, or on the VM of the task group that the optional `group` names, with the nested fleet that VM already has and no new VM. Requires Gateway access, an Idempotency-Key and a body with `command`, for example firewall:allow. The Gateway reads the cases file of the command, `swamp/proof/<family>/<action>.cases.yaml`, restores the base snapshot of the fleet, runs the cases and restores it again. A caller that is not a task VM and names no group gets proof.no_task_vm (409), a named group that does not exist tasks.group_missing (404), a group of another Project proof.wrong_project (409) and a group without its workspace tasks.no_workspace (409). The result holds command, file, outcome and one row for each case (program, command, case, verdict, seconds, and cause and failed for a failed case). The operation ends failed with proof.cases_failed when a case failed, proof.run_failed when no case ran, and proof.restore_failed when every case passed but the last restore failed, so the VM keeps a dirty fleet. Retry a lost reply with the same key. See /cli/proof/proof.

request_id.description: The request ID the Gateway assigned or accepted; the same value is in the `X-Orbit-Request-Id` response header and in the Activity record.

code.description: Stable error code, namespaced by family, such as `node.not_active` or `route.target_conflict`.

message.description: Safe message without credentials, environment values, or remote output.

details.description: Bounded, redacted details such as the conflicting record IDs or the failed validation rule.

kind.description: Always snapshot. after_sequence is accepted but does not request a delta.

entries.description: The recorded normalized transcript, oldest first. Output updates when a turn ends.

label.description: The role of a message, or the tool of an activity.

cursor.description: Always null. Reads do not resume a Pi stream.

archived.description: True when a stored transcript exists. A later turn can replace it.

agent.description: The agent liveness; while it is offline the answer is possibly outdated. Null on a Node without an observing agent.
